market_holds: Spot about $14.94-15.07 at 18:09 UTC (sealed baseline; Yahoo bars). Options: event-implied move 8.1% (straddle 12.9% to the 20 Nov expiry, ATM IV 104%, spread 59% of mid so it is only indicative), skew balanced (-1.9 vol points), put/call OI 0.8. Two prior prints, both down next session (-2.7% Q1 bmo, -6.5% Q2 amc; the Q2 drop came despite a revenue beat of $49.8m against about $45.4m). Run-in: +18% over 5 sessions, and that came with the sector. HAWK went from 12.76 to 15.0 after 5 Nov, while BKSY went 16.77 to 23.5 on its 5 Nov beat-and-raise, PL 11.37 to 14.2, SPIR 7.71 to 9.3, RKLB 46 to 65, and SPY had a -4.4% day on 5 Nov then rebounded. Since the 13 Aug print HAWK is -39%, against BKSY -24%, PL -43%, SPIR -33% and RKLB -19%, so most of the slide is the space basket. Consensus per the Earnings Whispers preview of 4 Nov: Q3 revenue about $57.0m (Benzinga $56.6m), EPS -$0.03, and FY26 revenue $213.2m. That sits below the company's own FY26 guide of $215-220m (adj. EBITDA $30-36m), its first-ever guide, issued 13 Aug. Management guided Q3 adj. EBITDA 'similar to Q2' ($7.0m) with a ramp into Q4. Sell-side targets are about $31-34 (Jefferies $31, RBC $33, August cuts), roughly double spot, so they are stale. The lock-up was already released on 1-2 Sep. Insider sales were small: CEO 10b5-1 sale of 92k shares at $14.78 on 1 Oct, plus tax-withholding sales. Short interest is unavailable (NYSE listing, Nasdaq API refuses).
view: The print turns on one line: does management hold the $215-220m FY26 guide, and does Q3 revenue (about $57m consensus) show the second-half ramp has started? The two prior quarters were flat at $49.8m each and backlog shrank from $302.7m (Dec) to $285.0m (Mar) to $292.2m (Jun). The low end needs about $115.4m in H2. Management said only $82m of that sits in backlog and the rest is book-and-burn plus awards. Since then the public awards are: the NRO CRFCA selection (18 Aug, no value disclosed), about $18m of Middle East awards (24 Sep, timing of revenue not stated) and the Indian Navy deal (already counted). There is no large GCC award of the kind the CEO said was coming 'in the very near future'. Several things argue the guide holds. It is a newly public company's first guide, set three months ago with bankers' conservatism and with knowledge of the backlog. The US government ended FY26 in September on enacted funding, with no October shutdown because a CR runs to 11 Dec, after Q2 was hurt by shutdown and CR delays. Gulf demand was elevated through the Iran conflict. The closest peer (BKSY, 5 Nov) beat and raised for the second time. Several things argue a disappointment, or a 'hold the low end with a Q4 hockey stick' outcome that this stock has already punished once. Q3 EBITDA was guided flat. Backlog is likely to fall again if Q3 bookings trail revenue. The Q2 beat still drew a -6.5% day. Analysts' FY number already sits about $2m under the guide low, so a plain reaffirm is a mild positive surprise to consensus, and a cut to about $205-210m is only a modest negative one. With the stock at about 5x sales, 56% off its high and bullish sentiment reported at 20%, the asymmetry leans slightly up. But the +18% sector run-in of the last week raises the bar, and I cannot see Q3 revenue or bookings from outside. I lean a little toward up, not enough to act on.
unpriced: Possibly the gap between a FY consensus ($213.2m, per a 4 Nov preview) that sits below a three-month-old first guide ($215-220m) and a newly public company's strong incentive to hold that guide. I could not show that any data since August makes the guide more or less reachable: the only new public bookings are about $18m in the Middle East. So this is a lean, not a demonstrated gap.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is whether the FY26 guide is held and Q3 shows the ramp, and nothing public since August reveals Q3 revenue or bookings beyond an $18m Middle East award. The guide-hold prior and depressed sentiment lean up. Flat Q3 EBITDA guidance, shrinking backlog, a negative reaction to the last beat and a +18% sector run-in lean the other way. Below the 65 threshold, so no trade.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A FY26 revenue guide cut below $215m, or Q3 backlog falling below about $285m with no large GCC award named, would make a down open likely. A reaffirmed or raised guide with a named large international award would make an up open likely.

self_critique: The case for a stronger up call: a newly IPO'd company almost never cuts its first guide at the next print, the FY consensus is already below the guide, the stock is at half the IPO price with sentiment washed out, and the closest peer just beat and raised. A reaffirm could gap it 10-15%. The case for down: two of two prior prints fell, one of them on a beat. Q3 EBITDA was guided flat and backlog has shrunk two quarters out of three. The CEO's 'very near future' GCC awards have not appeared publicly beyond $18m. The +18% sector run-in in five sessions means a merely in-line print can be sold. The two sides roughly offset, which is why I stay near 50.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped most: it showed that the 5-day rally and most of the post-August slide were the space basket, not HAWK. P7's 'estimate the line from its inputs' was useful but the inputs here (bookings, Q3 revenue) are mostly invisible from outside for a defence-intelligence vendor with classified US customers, so the answer stays near 50.
